title: Cartagena vs Havana: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Cartagena for ease, food, and beaches. Havana for a singular, unforgettable cultural experience. Both are world-class — choose based on your tolerance for adventure.

categories.name: Daily Budget
categories.summary: Both ~$60-100/day but Cartagena uses cards; Havana requires all-cash planning.

categories.name: Architecture & History
categories.summary: Cartagena is immaculately restored; Havana is grander and more layered.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Cartagena's Caribbean seafood and fine dining wins clearly.

categories.name: Music & Nightlife
categories.summary: Havana's live son cubano and salsa culture is unmatched in the Caribbean.

categories.name: Ease of Travel
categories.summary: Cartagena has Uber, ATMs, WiFi. Havana is cash-only with limited connectivity.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Islas del Rosario are excellent; Havana has no city beach.

categories.name: Cultural Depth
categories.summary: Havana is a living time capsule unlike anywhere else on Earth.

categories.name: Safety
categories.summary: Havana has lower violent crime; Cartagena needs vigilance outside the Old City.

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: Cartagena is a major hub; Cuba has US travel restrictions.

faq.question: Is Cartagena or Havana better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Cartagena is easier and more accessible. Havana is more unique but requires preparation.

faq.question: Which is cheaper, Cartagena or Havana?
faq.answer: Both cost $60-100/day but Havana requires all cash brought in advance — no ATM access.

faq.question: Can I combine Cartagena and Havana in one trip?
faq.answer: Yes — allow 10-14 days total, connect through Bogotá or Panama City.
